source.title: Uncertainty-Based Method for Improving Poorly Labeled Segmentation Datasets

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests segmentation networks on simulated noisy masks and reports that they overfit noisy labels without correction, including a condition where overfitting happens very quickly. It studies noisy pixel-level annotations rather than completely random image labels.
record.gate_note: The paper's abstract and introduction cite the random-label memorization finding from prior work. That cited result is not this study's result. Its own results test training with simulated noisy segmentation masks and uncertainty-based correction; rows below cover the relevant noisy-label outcomes. No results test random labels or unstructured inputs.
record.test_reason: Section 3.2 reports learning dynamics bearing on V6 in a new setting: binary medical-image segmentation with corrupted mask boundaries. Clean-mask accuracy peaks early and then drops as the networks overfit noisy masks. Table 1 does not test V4's random-corruption sweep or perfect training fit.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: predictive uncertainty can identify noisy pixel labels, and automatic relabeling improves segmentation and produces cleaner masks. The authors also report weaker relabeling performance for triangular liver masks because overfitting develops very quickly.
record.recipe_differences: Binary image segmentation with simulated noisy pixel-level mask boundaries; uses uncertainty estimation and mask relabeling rather than random image-label fitting.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and simulated mask shape/noise condition; the paper reports particularly fast overfitting for triangular liver masks.

fits_no_version.finding: Without correction, test Dice is higher against corrupted masks than clean masks in all six conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Segmentation networks trained on systematic boundary distortions can reproduce those distortions on held-out images.

fits_no_version.finding: Uncertainty-based relabeling improves clean-mask test Dice in all six conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Correcting uncertain pixel labels can improve segmentation trained with inaccurate boundaries.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
record.problems: Noise is simulated through boundary-mask approximations rather than completely random image labels. The paper reports Dice scores but no uncertainty intervals. Training error and chance-level test error are not reported. It notes fast overfitting on triangular liver masks.
record.rows_left_out: None; all reported Table 1 clean/noisy-mask results without correction and with the proposed relabeling method are included.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true and random labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Random corruption fractions from none to all, perfect training fit throughout, and steadily worsening test error toward chance.
Effects of explicit regularization on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Completely random labels and direct tracking of individual clean versus corrupted labels being memorized; the evidence concerns aggregate segmentation learning curves.

missing.what: Add learning-curve results for both datasets: clean-mask accuracy peaks early, around epoch 2 for dermatoscopy and epoch 1 for liver CT, then declines with noisy-mask overfitting. These temporal results are absent from the endpoint Dice rows.

record.verdict_notes: The cited random-label memorization result is prior work. This study's own temporal evidence bears on V6; its endpoint Dice comparisons do not establish random-label memorization, perfect training fit, or V4's corruption-fraction relationship.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random image labels, near-zero training error, test error at chance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training time for random versus true labels and how convergence changes with the fraction of corrupted labels.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.

The paper tests simulated noisy mask boundaries, not a sweep from none to all labels randomly corrupted; it does not report perfect training fit throughout such a sweep or steadily rising test error toward chance.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation affect random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy or random labels are memorized.
